correctness.rationale: For rank-one u⊗v with orthogonal unit vectors the radius is 1/2, and w((Au)⊗v)=(||Au||+|⟨Au,v⟩|)/2 by the standard rank-one numerical radius formula (compress to the span of the two vectors). Optimizing v gives the norm of the perpendicular component. For any square-zero B, the block form relative to ker B and its orthogonal complement gives w(B)=||B||/2, also when the block norm is approached only by a sequence. For each x with Bx≠0 replace B by ||B|| times the rank-one operator from the normalized ker(B)⊥ component of x to Bx/||Bx||. The factors are orthogonal, the radius is preserved, and the new value on x dominates the old in absolute value after multiplication by A. With ||A||=1, functional calculus gives q=⟨A²u,u⟩≤(1+r)s−r for s=⟨Au,u⟩, and q−s²≤(1−s)(s−r). Both terms of the rank-one objective increase in q at fixed s. Put s=r+(1−r)t; disjoint spectral slices approaching both endpoints supply all the required limiting two-point weights, irrespective of eigenvalue attainment. At r=1 the normalized operator is I. For r<1 strict concavity and the one-sided slopes give the unique interior maximizer and the derivative equation. At r=0 the root is t=3/4, with derivative of the optimum in r equal to −√3/4 by differentiating at that nondegenerate maximum. Near r=1 the profile expands uniformly as 1+(1−r)[t−1+√(t(1−t))]+O((1−r)²); the bracket has a unique maximizer at (1+1/√2)/2. A t just below 1 gives C(r)>1 for r<1; convex decomposition of A into rI plus the positive r=0 part gives C(r)≤r+(1−r)C(0) for r>0. For rank-one exact attainment with r<1, equality in the nonnegative functional-calculus defect (A−rI)(I−A) forces spectral support at both endpoints because the maximizing weight is interior; endpoint eigenvectors also suffice. This does not rule out higher-rank attainment without endpoint eigenvectors. The uploaded numerical check was read but not run; it does not certify the Hilbert-space result.

equivalent_formulations.reasoning: For w(B)≤1, Ando writes B=2(I−Z)^(1/2)D Z^(1/2), 0≤Z≤I and ||D||≤1. Cauchy–Schwarz and the arithmetic–geometric mean bound a unit-vector matrix element by 1+Tr[Z(xx*−yy*)]≤1+√(1−|⟨x,y⟩|²), since the rank-two difference has opposite eigenvalues ±√(1−|⟨x,y⟩|²). Applying it to x and Ax/||Ax|| gives the same envelope as the frozen rank-one lower bound. The resulting unrestricted formulation was derived in the review, not found as a prior fixed-band theorem.

The sharpness construction and infinite-dimensional attainment distinction add substance beyond a numerical interpolation or the universal endpoint.
